feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for a senior digital communications leader: the experience is relevant, progressive, and supported by concrete platforms, scope, and outcomes. It is generally clear and polished, but it feels slightly dense and repetitive, with some structural overlap that reduces impact.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership trajectory within NACo, showing progression from coordinator to director and reinforcing credibility in public-sector digital communications.  
- Good use of scale and specificity: 10,000+ pages, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ publishers, and named tools/platforms strengthen impact.  
- Writing is professional and consistent overall, with strong domain positioning around Drupal, analytics, governance, multimedia, and AI-enabled search.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce duplication across Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; consolidate to create a tighter structure and make key differentiators stand out faster.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially in the freelance role and older positions; quantify improvements in engagement, efficiency, adoption, or campaign performance where possible.  
- Minor style/consistency issues: “social, and multimedia” has an unnecessary comma; “A2/Learning” is awkwardly formatted; capitalization/style varies slightly across sections (“AI-enabled”/tool naming, “Topline Skills” vs. “Core Competencies”). No obvious misspellings or major grammar errors.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning with clear seniority and public-sector focus. However, it overlaps heavily with the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience, and could be sharper by foregrounding scale and outcomes.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and reduce list-like phrasing; replace “platforms, governance models and content operations” with more direct language.
- Add 1–2 concrete scale signals from recent roles (for example, 10,000+ pages, 3.5M annual page views, 50+ publishers) to increase impact.
- Recast the second sentence to emphasize leadership outcomes, not just scope: modernization, governance, analytics, and AI-enabled discovery.
- Suggested rewrite: Digital platform and communications leader with 12+ years of experience modernizing high-volume public-sector web ecosystems. Leads enterprise website transformation, digital governance, analytics infrastructure, editorial operations, and AI-enabled content discovery for complex, mission-driven organizations, including platforms serving 3.5M annual page views and 50+ internal publishers.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “content discovery” is more specific and less repetitive.
- “Senior digital leader” is close to the subtitle; vary the wording to avoid repetition.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be sharper if phrased more distinctly and weighted toward strategic leadership rather than repeating adjacent sections.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Tighten and standardize phrasing for parallel structure; use concise noun phrases throughout.
- Emphasize higher-value, recent strengths: enterprise web modernization, governance, analytics, AI-enabled discovery, and workflow integration.
- Consider this rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboards, and reporting infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel communications leadership • Public-sector advocacy communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations
- If space allows elsewhere, reserve more tactical items like “livestream operations” for Topline Skills or Technical + IT.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled search and content experiences” and “Workflow automation and platform integration” repeat Topline Skills/Technical + IT language.
- “Multi-channel communications operations” and “Advocacy and public-sector communications” also echo the header and Topline Skills.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it currently repeats themes already covered in Work Experience and reads a bit dense for a footer. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes or scope will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp, parallel sentence.
- Use consistent action/result structure: “Built/Developed/Launched X to achieve Y.”
- Tighten wording: e.g., “hybrid retrieval, vector search, and bill-level AI chat” and “10-by-20-foot” for style consistency.
- If possible, add one concrete outcome, audience, or scale detail to 1–2 projects to increase impact.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite work, anniversary campaign, and advocacy video series all overlap with current/future role bullets; consider reframing as “selected examples” rather than restating responsibilities.
- “Built” appears repeatedly; vary with “Launched,” “Developed,” or “Produced” for better rhythm.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: colemandavis4@gmail.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with good strategic/technical range, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your NACo entries and topline skills. Tighten it around the highest-value consulting outcomes, especially what is new: enterprise improvement, Drupal delivery, and AI-enabled search.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client value: “Advise a U.S. national membership organization on digital strategy, enterprise web improvement, and cross-channel content operations.”
- Replace generic bullets with sharper outcome-oriented phrasing: “Built digital workflows, analytics, and governance models to improve coordination across web, email, social, and multimedia teams.”
- Combine Drupal/CMS points: “Designed and implemented Drupal campaign experiences, including microsites, modular content components, member toolkits, and front-end/CMS enhancements for large public-facing sites.”
- Keep the AI work as the differentiator: “Lead an AI-enabled search initiative, defining retrieval strategy, structured content requirements, and user-facing discovery experience.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, workflows, analytics” repeats language already used in NACo roles; use this item to emphasize consulting impact and current technical execution.
- Avoid restating broad cross-channel leadership already covered in the summary and core competencies.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale signals. It would be sharper if the opening were less list-like and if each bullet emphasized outcomes, team leadership, and transformation rather than channel ownership alone.

Suggested edit
- Replace the opening with a tighter summary: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget strategy for a national association.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground impact: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal site serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel management more outcome-based: add growth, engagement, deliverability, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements if available; otherwise trim vague audience-size phrasing.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built NACo’s analytics and governance infrastructure across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving reporting, publishing standards, and cross-department planning.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role; keep this entry focused on enterprise leadership and transformation.
- Video studio language may partially overlap with earlier video-production bullets; emphasize building institutional capacity, not routine production.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story and good scope, but this entry overlaps heavily with the later NACo director role and earlier manager/producer role. Make it more distinct by emphasizing executional leadership, channel ownership, and any concrete growth or process outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite the lead to focus on operational ownership: “Directed day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social media, and video, coordinating editorial execution and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Tighten bullets and use stronger verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching [X]+ county officials and public-sector stakeholders” and “Produced a weekly advocacy video series that established video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Add measurable outcomes if available: newsletter open/click rates, audience growth, publishing volume, turnaround time, or cross-team adoption of planning processes.
- Replace “helped” phrasing with direct contribution: “Standardized editorial planning and digital publishing workflows, improving consistency and cross-department coordination.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthened editorial planning/workflows” overlaps with the 2022–2024 NACo role; keep this version more tactical and execution-focused.
- Weekly video/newsletter language also appears in the 2015–2018 role; avoid repeating “first” or origin-story framing here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it overlaps heavily with the header, Core Competencies, and recent NACo bullets. Make it sharper, more senior, and more distinct by emphasizing enterprise leadership and governance rather than generic communications phrasing.

Suggested edit
- Replace with tighter, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & transformation
- Editorial governance & content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, policy & advocacy messaging
- Audience strategy & content planning
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to align with the header while sounding more executive.
- “Audience-focused content planning” is weaker than the others; strengthen it with “Audience strategy” or “Audience segmentation & content planning.”
- If space allows, use parallel noun phrases only; avoid mixing broad functions with softer descriptors.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Multi-channel communication” already appear in Core Competencies and the header.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” closely repeats “Policy & advocacy communication”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster, but it reads as a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform execution and modernization themes tied to recent work.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool inventory to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint & Power Pages administration; CMS modernization; front-end implementation (HTML/CSS/JavaScript/jQuery); API integrations; workflow automation; Airtable-based systems; AI-enabled search.”
- Put strongest/recent differentiators earlier: Drupal, CMS modernization, AI-enabled search, API integrations.
- Tighten wording: change “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” to “Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery).”
- If space allows, add one impact cue: “enterprise CMS modernization” or “large public-facing web platforms.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT.” Keep Topline Skills strategic/capability-based and leave full tool detail to Technical + IT.
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” also overlap with Core Competencies and Automation & Workflow Systems.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tools list, but it reads as a software inventory rather than a value-focused skills line. Since the NACo Director role already names these platforms, this item should emphasize analytical outcomes and decision support.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tool list to capability-led phrasing, e.g.: “Digital analytics & optimization: GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio, Power BI, Microsoft Clarity; KPI framework design; executive/leadership reporting; SEO and performance analysis.”
- Put the highest-value capabilities first: analytics strategy, KPI design, reporting, optimization; tools second.
- Consider replacing “Leadership reporting” with “Executive reporting” or “Decision-ready reporting” for sharper phrasing.
- If supported elsewhere, add an outcome cue such as “performance measurement and optimization” or “insight generation for strategic decisions.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps with “Data analytics & reporting” in Core Competencies and the NACo Director bullet on expanding analytics infrastructure.
- Avoid overemphasizing tools here if they are already covered in work experience; use this section to summarize capability breadth.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong supporting skill area, but it reads generic and overlaps with “Multimedia & live event production” in Core Competencies and multiple NACo bullets. Make it more specific to current/recent capability and operational scope.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as outcome-oriented, higher-signal skills: “Broadcast video production • Livestream and hybrid event delivery • PTZ camera and studio system operation • Virtual event technical production”
- Consider replacing “Video production and editing” with “Broadcast-quality video production” to align with the in-house studio achievement.
- Tighten “Hybrid and virtual event production” to “Hybrid/virtual event technical production” for clearer ownership.
- If accurate, add scale/tool context instead of generic terms, e.g. “Multi-camera livestream production” or “Studio build-out and operations.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item overlaps with Core Competencies: “Multimedia & live event production”; keep one broader and one more technical.
- “Studio operations” and “livestreaming” are already evidenced in NACo roles, so avoid repeating identical phrasing elsewhere.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills almost exactly. This item should either add nuance (depth/level) or be tightened to emphasize the most credible, recent platforms.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by strongest/recent evidence: “Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages” is fine, but consider signaling depth: “Drupal (enterprise, migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages.”
- If space allows, add proficiency framing rather than just a list: “Enterprise CMS platforms: Drupal, WordPress, SharePoint, Power Pages; static publishing via GitHub Pages.”
- Prioritize Drupal since it is the clearest recent platform in work history and projects.
- If you want more impact, replace weaker/less-evidenced tools with versions or scope only where true, e.g., “Drupal 10” or “10,000+ page migration.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This is highly redundant with “Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution,” which already lists the same platforms.
- GitHub Pages is not supported elsewhere in the CV; remove it if it was not materially used recently.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, relevant stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools that support recent Drupal, analytics, automation, and AI/search work.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Front-End, Integration & DevOps Tools” to distinguish it from platform/CMS skills.
- Rewrite as: “HTML5/CSS3 • JavaScript/jQuery • API and tag integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions (deployment/workflow automation)”
- If accurate, add one higher-value modern detail tied to recent work, e.g. “custom Drupal front-end implementation,” “search/retrieval integrations,” or “serverless scripting.”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless other skills also use versioning; “HTML/CSS” is cleaner.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already appear in Topline Skills; keep them in one place or make this section more tool-specific.
- “Workflow automation” is covered elsewhere; avoid implying the same capability again via GitHub Actions unless framed as deployment/CI.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow automation capability. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize capability, e.g. “Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools.”
- Group by function for faster scanning: “Automation: Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Project/work management: Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Collaboration: Slack, Microsoft Teams.”
- If accurate, add a light qualifier to show applied use: “used to build editorial planning, approvals, reporting, and cross-team coordination workflows.”
- Keep only the strongest, most relevant tools if space is tight; Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Teams likely carry more weight than Basecamp/Trello.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Airtable” and “workflow automation” already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Slack and Teams are common collaboration tools; they add less differentiation unless grouped concisely.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Clear and relevant, but it reads as a generic tool list. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize platform depth and audience engagement systems rather than repeat “email newsletters.”

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten the list to: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add a qualifier for scale or use case: **Enterprise/member communications, newsletter operations, journey-based campaigns**
- Consider a stronger version if space allows: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights/Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp • enterprise email operations and member engagement workflows**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters” or “tens of thousands of recipients” here; that impact is already covered in the NACo experience bullets.
- Be careful not to overlap with “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies unless you add platform-specific context.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is highly duplicative of “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization.” In this section, make it more technical and specific, not another generic capability list.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as a tighter tools-focused line: “GA4 • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Microsoft Clarity • Google Search Console • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding”
- Replace “SEO” with “Google Search Console” or “technical SEO analysis” to make it more concrete and tool-aligned.
- Change “Dashboarding” to “KPI dashboarding” or “executive reporting dashboards” for clearer business value.
- Order by strongest/recently evidenced tools first: GA4, BigQuery, Power BI, Looker Studio, Clarity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps almost exactly with “Topline Skills > Analytics, Insights & Optimization”; consider trimming one version or using this section for tools only and the Topline section for outcomes/capabilities.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced elsewhere; keep it only if you can support it in recent roles.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the stronger 2018–2024 NACo entries. Make it more foundational and execution-focused, with any concrete scale or outputs you can quantify.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe as early-career buildout: “Promoted across two digital roles to help establish NACo’s first in-house digital team…”
- Emphasize distinct contributions: website refresh, livestream/event production, recurring video content, and junior staff support.
- Add measurable outcomes where possible: number of livestreams/events produced, frequency of video updates, audience growth, email/social volume, or workflow time saved.
- Possible rewrite: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team. Supported a major website refresh, produced recurring livestreams and weekly video updates for member communications, and improved day-to-day workflows across web, email, social and multimedia. Provided direct guidance to a digital media associate, helping expand internal production capacity.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Weekly video updates” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on launching/building the capability.
- Avoid repeating governance/operations language already covered more strongly in later roles.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry that shows progression into digital/media work, but it reads broadly and overlaps with later NACo roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting county-focused programs and policy priorities, while contributing digital and multimedia content across organizational communications.”
- Make the second sentence sharper: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- If accurate, add scope or output: number of episodes launched, audiences served, or types of research/projects supported.
- Remove filler like “contributed to” where possible; use stronger verbs such as “produced,” “developed,” or “launched.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid repeating broad digital content/multimedia language already covered more strongly in the 2015–2018 and later NACo roles.
- Don’t overstate team leadership here; later roles already establish that progression.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful supporting skills, but this item is currently a mixed list of software and capabilities, and it overlaps with stronger, more recent multimedia leadership already shown in work experience and Topline Skills. Tighten it into a clean tools-focused entry.

Suggested edit:
